chunks: I wrote to him (peace be upon him) that the ones before us are differing regarding tawhid.
He said: So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Glory be to the One Who cannot be limited nor described. There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.'

key_terms.التوحيد: Tawhid — Islamic doctrine of divine unity and uniqueness
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ: Glorification formula — expressing God's absolute transcendence
key_terms.يُحَدُّ: To be limited or bounded — what God transcends absolutely
key_terms.يُوصَفُ: To be described or attributed — what exceeds human conception of God

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about describing God's nature in Islam?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qasani wrote to the Imam reporting that members of his community were engaged in disputes about divine unity (tawhid). The Imam's written response affirms God's absolute transcendence using both negative theology (apophatic: God cannot be limited or described) and positive divine attributes drawn directly from Quran 42:11 (All-Hearing, All-Seeing). This response reflects the Shia theological position that while God's essence is beyond all human description, His self-disclosed attributes in scripture are valid.
